articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations today targeting individuals and entities involved in counter narcotics and counter terrorism activities.
These actions aim to disrupt the financial networks of those who support illicit drug trafficking and terrorist organizations globally, reinforcing international efforts to combat these threats.
Further details regarding the specific individuals and entities designated, as well as the implications of these actions, are available on the Treasury website.

articles.headline: OFAC Updates Iran Designations Amid Heightened Tensions
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued an update to its Iran designations, reflecting ongoing efforts to exert economic pressure on the Iranian regime.

This action comes as senior Iranian officials express concerns about potential further military strikes or an intensified economic stranglehold by the U.S., which they believe could force Tehran into retaliatory measures.
The updated designations are part of a broader strategy to disrupt Iranian financial networks and its proliferation-sensitive nuclear activities and ballistic missile program.

articles.headline: New Iran-related Designations Announced by OFAC
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations, continuing its campaign of economic pressure against the Iranian regime.
These designations target individuals and entities deemed to be supporting Iran's destabilizing activities, including its nuclear program and regional proxies.
The action underscores the U.S. commitment to preventing Iran from acquiring weapons of mass destruction and supporting terrorism.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Cyber-related, Transnational Criminal, and Cuba Designations; Publishes Cuba Determination
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a series of designations targeting cyber-related activities, transnational criminal organizations, and entities linked to Cuba.

The U.S. also issued a determination under Executive Order 14404, authorizing sanctions against foreign persons operating in Cuba's electronics, manufacturing, marine, and technology sectors, effective November 5.
These actions are part of a comprehensive push to counter the Cuban regime's malign activities and illicit revenue networks, including those supporting its oil shipping and military supply chains.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / ABA Banking Journal / CTV News / U.S. Department of State

articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Iran-related Designations, Alert, and Amended Venezuela GL
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations and published an alert titled 'Iranian Shadow Fleet Reliance on False Flags for Sanctions Evasion.'
The alert warns of sanctions risks associated with dealing with potentially false-flagged vessels used by Iran to transport petroleum, including those operating on behalf of the Iranian military.

Additionally, OFAC issued Venezuela-related General License 5AA, authorizing certain transactions related to the Petróleos de Venezuela, S.A. 2020 8.5 Percent Bond on or after December 18, 2026, and amended FAQ 595 to reflect this update.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / The Hindu / ABA Banking Journal / Anadolu Ajansı

Stakeholders are advised to review the updated General License for specific details and compliance requirements.

articles.region: North Korea, Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities in North Korea and Democratic Republic of the Congo
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations targeting entities in North Korea and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

These actions aim to counter threats posed by North Korea's weapons of mass destruction programs and human rights abuses, as well as to address corruption and instability in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
The designations underscore the U.S. commitment to promoting peace, security, and human rights globally.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking and Rejecting Transactions and Filing Reports
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued amended Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) regarding blocking and rejecting transactions and filing reports with OFAC.
These amendments provide updated guidance and clarifications for financial institutions and other entities on their compliance obligations under OFAC regulations.
The updated FAQs are crucial for ensuring accurate reporting and adherence to sanctions requirements.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran-related, Russia-related General Licenses; Removes Belarus, North Korea Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related and Russia-related General Licenses, providing authorizations for certain transactions.
Concurrently, OFAC removed several designations related to Belarus and North Korea, indicating a recalibration of sanctions policies in these areas.
The agency also issued amended Frequently Asked Questions to provide further guidance on these changes and other sanctions-related matters.

articles.headline: UK Adds 20 Entities to Russia Sanctions List, Targets Energy Sector
body: On November 12, 2026, the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office updated the UK Sanctions List with 20 new additions and one variation under the Russia sanctions regime.

Among the designated entities is JSC NIPIGAZPERERABOTKA (NIPIGAZ), which the Secretary of State considers to be involved in obtaining a benefit from or supporting the Government of Russia by operating in the Russian energy sector.

The updated sanctions also include transport prohibitions, where a ship owned, controlled, chartered, or operated by a designated person is prohibited from entering a UK port and may face detention or refusal of registration.

articles.headline: BIS Streamlines Export Controls for Sound Suppressors
body: The Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) announced that, as of November 20, 2026, the export of certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors will be subject to BIS's Export Administration Regulations (EAR), rather than the State Department's U.S. Munitions List.

This deregulatory action aligns export controls on suppressors with those already applied to firearms, aiming to alleviate compliance burdens on the firearms industry while maintaining national security.

Under this new rule, suppressors will be added to the Commerce Control List (CCL), and a license will be required for certain exports, reexports, or in-country transfers, with applicable license exceptions for firearms also extending to suppressors.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.
